hook.text: A factory dumps waste into a river. The factory saves money. Downstream farmers lose their crops. Nobody sent a bill.

buildup.text: An externality is a cost or benefit imposed on someone who did not agree to it. Pollution is the classic example.

discovery.text: Externalities can be positive too. A neighbor's beautiful garden raises your property value at no cost to you.

twist.text: Markets fail without pricing externalities. When pollution is free, companies overproduce it. The cost is just hidden.

climax.text: Look for hidden externalities in every deal. Someone always pays for the unpriced costs—they just may not know it.

punchline.text: If you can't see who pays the cost, it might be you.

quiz.question: What is a negative externality?
options: A cost imposed on someone who didn't agree to it
A cost that a company pays voluntarily
